newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania monolith setting for Miss Europe glitz.
newsitem.headline: Albania monolith setting for Miss Europe glitz.

text.p: Albania's Palace of Congresses, the huge concrete monolith built to the glory of everlasting communism, sheds its grey past for a new glitzy image on Saturday as the setting for Miss Europe '96.
The annual beauty pageant, usually held in a fashionable city of Western Europe, is being staged for the first time in what was once the continent's most isolated Stalinist state.
The contest, featuring 35 contestants from across Europe, begins at 8.30 p.m. local time (1830 GMT).
Situated on Tirana's main tree-lined boulevard, the Palace of Congresses once echoed with the teachings of Marx and the thoughts of Albania's post-World War Two dictator Enver Hoxha.
Sober-suited communist apparatchiks were summoned to the cavernous building once a year for the congress of Albania's Party of Labour to applaud the policies of hardline leaders.

The contrast on Saturday evening will be stark. The audience is more likely to be overpowered by the click of high-heeled shoes and the waft of perfume and hair-spray than the dialectics of Kant and Hegel.
"Could we have ever imagined that European beauty queens would walk right here? Never." said a man called Rrapi after Friday night's dress rehearsal.

The off-white marble construction was completed 10 years ago, a year after Hoxha's death. His successor, Ramiz Alia, was the first party leader to address delegates there in 1986 in what was called "the congress of continuation".
He was Albania's last communist president. A popular revolt toppled his regime in 1990. Alia now awaits trial on charges of ordering the shooting of Albanians who tried to flee the state.
Little of that will be on the minds of spectators on Saturday, as they view contestants parade in traditional folk costume, swim-suits and evening gowns.

Gone are the days when prudish communist officials banned fashion, gambling and rock music as capitalist decadence. French band Gypsy Kings and Italian blues king Zucchero will be on hand to entertain the well-dressed, coiffured audience during the intervals.
In a video-link with the United States, actor Jim Belushi, partly of Albanian ancestry, is scheduled to send his greetings.
The contest will cap a two-week stay in Albania by the contestants, many of whom were somewhat nervous of competing in a country which they knew little about.
Despite the few roads, primitive communications and poorly-maintained infrastructure, most have been won over after touring the countryside and Adriatic coast.
"Next year I think I'll come for my holidays here," said American Tracy Kemble, Mrs Globe '96-97, who will compere the pageant, choreographed by France's Jean-Paul Plouvier.

With tickets priced between $30 to $50, a place in the 3,000-seat auditorium will be out of the reach of most Albanians. But broadcasters say the whole country will be watching the contest live on Albanian state television.
